# Instructions for accurately documenting results that contradict the hypothesis in a psychology research report

1. Start with the research records.
2.
completion: Summarise earlier, similar studies, including findings that support or invalidate the hypothesis. 3. Summarise the hypothesis to refresh the test group’s memories. 4. Remind the test group that the results were not what they expected, then outline the reasons why. # Example 409: Results: Research records ## Data points that do not support the hypothesis – a screenshot of all data points in an analysis, including the result I want to document as unusually benign, such as an innocuous message or a message that is not assertive enough. 1. [Annotate each data point with a reference to its relevance, or to explain how it does not invalidate the hypothesis](https://www.instagram.com/p/CfqQfQvpY6g/). Or, if there is more than one plausible reason for its existence, reference all hypotheses.
